content:
{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Inconsistent patient numbers in synopsis",
      "quote": "Approximately 120 patients will be treated in this study, with a maximum of approximately 20 patients per tumor type",
      "page": 8,
      "section": "1.1 Synopsis",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "critical",
      "explanation": "The synopsis states 120 patients will be treated, but later in the same section and in the statistical methods it says 'Approximately 100 patients will be treated' and 'a global target of 100 patients treated'. This discrepancy is critical for sample size and feasibility.",
      "fix": "Reconcile the number of patients to be treated; likely change 120 to 100 or clarify if 120 is a different population (e.g., enrolled)."
    },
    {
      "title": "Cross-reference to non-existent section",
      "quote": "Intervention after the end of the study is described in Section 99.7.",
      "page": 8,
      "section": "1.1 Synopsis",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "critical",
      "explanation": "Section 99.7 does not exist in the protocol; this is a placeholder that leaves post-trial access undefined, which is a required element (M11 4.5).",
      "fix": "Replace with the correct section number or add the post-trial access description in the appropriate section."
    },
    {
      "title": "Primary endpoint lacks estimand details",
      "quote": "To assess the efficacy of T-DXd in patients with Confirmed ORR according to RECIST v1.1, as metastatic or unresectable tumors harboring specific assessed by ICR. HER2 activating mutations across tumor types.",
      "page": 8,
      "section": "1.1 Synopsis",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The primary objective/endpoint is stated but no estimand is defined (e.g., intercurrent events handling, population-level summary). M11 3.1 requires associated estimand(s).",
      "fix": "Add a formal estimand for the primary endpoint, including handling of intercurrent events like treatment discontinuation or death."
    },
    {
      "title": "Interim futility rule conflicts with measurable disease requirement",
      "quote": "Enrolment in a specific tumor type will be paused after 8 patients with Investigator-assessed measurable disease at baseline have been treated within that tumor type",
      "page": 8,
      "section": "1.1 Synopsis",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The MDAS definition says 'All patients will have Investigator-assessed measurable disease at baseline according to inclusion criteria', but the inclusion criteria are not provided in the synopsis. If measurable disease is an inclusion criterion, then all treated patients are in MDAS, making the 8-patient rule redundant. If not, the rule is unclear.",
      "fix": "Clarify whether measurable disease is an inclusion criterion and align the MDAS definition and futility rule accordingly."
    },
    {
      "title": "No Data Monitoring Committee but interim futility evaluations planned",
      "quote": "There will be no Data Monitoring Committee for this study.",
      "page": 8,
      "section": "1.1 Synopsis",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The study plans interim futility evaluations per tumor type, but no DMC is mentioned. It is unclear who will perform these evaluations and how they will be overseen, which is a governance gap (M11 11.2).",
      "fix": "Specify the oversight body for interim futility evaluations (e.g., sponsor, independent statistician) and their responsibilities."
    },
    {
      "title": "Contraception requirements not described",
      "quote": "Patients will be enrolled at approximately 20 sites globally. Adult patients with unresectable and/or metastatic solid tumors carrying pre-specified HER2 activating mutations",
      "page": 8,
      "section": "1.1 Synopsis",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The synopsis does not mention contraception requirements for patients of reproductive potential, which is a required element (M11 5.4) and critical for a drug with potential teratogenicity.",
      "fix": "Add a section on contraception requirements for males and females, including duration and methods."
    },
    {
      "title": "Sample size justification incomplete",
      "quote": "A sample size of 100 patients has been determined to provide sufficient precision for the estimation of the ORR in this population",
      "page": 8,
      "section": "1.1 Synopsis",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The sample size section provides CI for observed ORRs but does not state the assumed true ORR, the target precision, or the power for any hypothesis test. This is insufficient for a rigorous sample size determination (SPIRIT 19).",
      "fix": "Provide the assumed ORR, the desired CI width, and the rationale for the 100-patient target, including any power calculations."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inconsistent follow-up durations",
      "quote": "until all patients have had the opportunity for approximately 44 weeks of follow-up after treatment assignment. This will provide at least 6 months of follow-up from the anticipated median time of first response assessment.",
      "page": 8,
      "section": "1.1 Synopsis",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The synopsis states 44 weeks of follow-up for efficacy, but later says the final analysis for DoR is planned when the last patient has had 32 weeks of follow-up. These durations are inconsistent and may confuse the analysis timing.",
      "fix": "Clarify the follow-up duration for the primary analysis vs. the final DoR analysis, and ensure they are consistent."
    }
  ]
}
